TinyML Keyword Spotting

This sample demonstrates a streaming keyword spotting (KWS) wake-word engine on the RTL87x2G. Instead of a live microphone, it drives the model with a static PCM clip embedded in the firmware: the clip is passed through the TinyML mel-spectrogram feature frontend and then into a streaming TFLite quantized model that detects the wake word hi_realtek.

Unlike a one-shot classifier, the model is streaming: the embedded 16 kHz clip is fed to the mel frontend one 10 ms frame at a time, and the model is invoked every 30 ms (3 frames). The model keeps its own internal ring-buffer state between invocations, so each call advances the audio stream by 30 ms and outputs the current wake-word probability. The sample walks the whole clip step by step, prints the probability trajectory, and reports a wake event when the probability stays above the threshold for several consecutive steps.

Building and Downloading

The project path of this sample is as follows:

Project file: samples\tinyml\tinyml_kws\proj\rtl87x2g\mdk

Project file: samples\tinyml\tinyml_kws\proj\rtl87x2g\gcc

Follow the steps below to build and run this sample:

  1. Open the project file.

  2. To build the target, follow the steps listed on the Generating App Image in Quick Start.

  3. After a successful build, the app bin app_MP_xxx.bin is generated under mdk\bin or gcc\bin.

  4. To download the app bin into the EVB, follow the steps listed on the MP Tool Download in Quick Start.

  5. Press the reset button to start running.

Test Verification

  1. After the EVB starts, observe the output in the Debug Analyzer tool. The actual CPU operating frequency is printed first.

    CPU actual clock is 125 MHz

  2. After the feature frontend and the inference engine are initialized, the sample prints the static-clip configuration and begins offline streaming.

    [TS] set_arena_size(80KB) ret=0
KWS offline start: 16000Hz, 48000 samples, 100 steps (30ms/step)

  3. While walking the clip, moderate scores are logged for debugging, and each step that stays above the threshold (default 80%) is counted as a pre-hit.

    [KWS] xx% step=50 inf=xxxxus
[KWS] pre-hit 1/3 hi_realtek (xx%) step=xx inf=xxxxus
[KWS] pre-hit 2/3 hi_realtek (xx%) step=xx inf=xxxxus

  4. Once the wake word is confirmed (enough consecutive hits, default 3), a wake event is printed. When the whole clip has been processed, a summary line reports the best score and whether the wake word fired.

    [KWS] *** WAKE UP*** hi_realtek (xx%) step=xx inf=xxxxus
[KWS] done: xx steps, best=xx%, wake=YES

Note

The feature frontend library and the TFLite model inference engine library need to be added to the project. The former encapsulates the mel feature frontend API; the latter encapsulates the TFLite model inference engine API.

  • libkws_feature.lib: encapsulates the mel feature frontend API.

  • libts_realtek_cm55.lib: encapsulates the TFLite model inference engine API.

  • libkws_feature.a: encapsulates the mel feature frontend API.

  • libts_realtek_gcc_cm55.a: encapsulates the TFLite model inference engine API.

Note

The model data used in the project is stored in the model_tflite.cpp file. It is a streaming quantized wake-word model with input int8[1, 3, 40] (3 time-steps × 40 mel channels) and a single uint8 wake-word probability output.

Note

The static test clip used to drive the model is stored in kws_sample_pcm.c as a 16 kHz mono int16 array (kws_sample_pcm[] with length kws_sample_pcm_len). The shipped clip is a real hi_realtek utterance (3.0 s, 48000 samples) captured on an RTL87x2G device from the same audio pipeline the model was trained on, so it reproduces a wake event out of the box. Replace it with your own recording of the wake word to test a different clip.

Initialization

  1. Set the CPU operating frequency to 125 MHz and initialize the DWT cycle counter.

  2. Initialize the mel feature frontend (KwsFrontendInit). The configuration is fixed to match the model's training pipeline (16 kHz sample rate, 30 ms window, 10 ms step, 40 mel channels, PCAN noise suppression enabled).

  3. Register the heap and the streaming model, set the tensor arena size, and call ts_realtek_init to build the interpreter once. The streaming state is preserved across all subsequent invocations.

    /* Feature frontend (fixed config, matches training). */
KwsFrontendInit(&s_fe);

/* Inference engine — initialised once, streaming state preserved. */
ts_realtek_register_heap(ts_malloc, ts_free);
ts_realtek_set_arena_size(80u * 1024u);
ts_realtek_register_model(get_model_pointer(), get_model_size());
ts_realtek_init();

Functional Implementation

A single application task walks the embedded static PCM clip and performs one streaming inference step every 30 ms of audio:

  1. Split the clip into 30 ms steps (480 int16 samples each). For each step, take a pointer directly into kws_sample_pcm[] — no ring buffer or DMA is involved.

  2. Feed the frontend three 10 ms frames (160 samples each). Each frame yields 40 uint16 mel energies, which are quantized to int8 using the training-time scale; the three frames form a 120-byte feature tensor.

  3. Feed the feature tensor into the TFLite streaming model. ts_realtek_invoke dequantizes the uint8 output internally and returns the wake-word probability in [0, 1].

  4. Apply detection logic: count consecutive steps above the threshold; when enough consecutive hits accumulate, report a wake event and track the best score.

  5. When the whole clip has been processed, print a summary, release the inference resources, and idle.

    Related macro definitions:

    #define KWS_SAMPLES_PER_STEP  480    /* samples per 30 ms inference step */
#define KWS_SAMPLES_PER_TICK  160    /* samples per 10 ms frame */
#define KWS_FRAMES_PER_STEP   3      /* frames per inference step */
#define KWS_NUM_CHANNELS      40     /* mel channels */
#define KWS_INP_ZP            (-128) /* int8 quantization zero-point */
#define KWS_THRESHOLD         0.80f  /* wake-word decision threshold (0-1) */
#define KWS_REQUIRED_HITS     3      /* consecutive hits required to fire */

    uint32_t num_steps = kws_sample_pcm_len / KWS_SAMPLES_PER_STEP;

for (uint32_t step = 0; step < num_steps; step++)
{
    const int16_t *step_pcm = kws_sample_pcm + step * KWS_SAMPLES_PER_STEP;

    /* Extract + quantize 3 mel frames into the int8 model input. */
    for (int f = 0; f < KWS_FRAMES_PER_STEP; f++)
    {
        size_t n_read = 0;
        KwsFrontendOutput out = KwsFrontendProcess(
                                    &s_fe,
                                    step_pcm + f * KWS_SAMPLES_PER_TICK,
                                    KWS_SAMPLES_PER_TICK, &n_read);
        for (int ch = 0; ch < KWS_NUM_CHANNELS; ch++)
        {
            s_features_int8[f * KWS_NUM_CHANNELS + ch] =
                (out.size == 0) ? (int8_t)KWS_INP_ZP
                                : quantize_feature(out.values[ch]);
        }
    }

    /* Streaming inference: probability of the wake word. */
    float prob = kws_engine_invoke(s_features_int8);

    if (prob >= KWS_THRESHOLD && ++consecutive_hits >= KWS_REQUIRED_HITS)
    {
        /* Wake fired for this clip. */
        woke = true;
        consecutive_hits = 0;
    }
}
